requirement:
A delivered read page records the dependencies retained by that page under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. Each continuation of a
node or mapped source read retains the original node identity and content
fingerprint; reading a later page does not observe a newer version. A change
to that node's fingerprint can invalidate the evidence even if it happens
between pages. Agent tools record on delivery. Discovery pages record no evidence
inputs, just like their initial result. Preparing an undelivered page records
no read.
rationale:
The marked tests cover each obligation of `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.pages.inputs`.

- **Delivered read pages record their dependencies, and agent tools record on delivery.** `graph_tools_record_delivered_snapshots_and_prepared_pages_do_not_record_delivery` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs` runs `read_node` and `get_next_page` through the agent. It asserts the resulting `Dependency::Node` has the full 18,000-character fingerprint. It also asserts `prepared_inputs` and `delivered_inputs` are (3, 3). `source_read_pages_retain_text_and_dependencies_without_another_read` asserts that every `get_next_page` delivery carries a `Dependency::Node` with the original fingerprint.
- **Continuations keep the original node identity and fingerprint, and never see a newer version.** `graph_read_pages_retain_the_prepared_snapshot_after_contents_change` changes the graph contents between pages, using `ChangingProvider`. It asserts the provider was read exactly once (`reads == [1]`). It asserts the only dependency is `Node(1)` with the original fingerprint. It asserts the concatenated pages equal the original text. `source_read_pages_retain_text_and_dependencies_without_another_read` overwrites the file after the first page. It asserts the continuation text and fingerprint stay the original and that the observation callback ran once. A continuation that re-read or re-fingerprinted would fail both tests. Because a change after the first read would not alter the recorded fingerprint, the "can invalidate evidence even if it happens between pages" clause is a consequence of this retention and needs no separate test.
- **Discovery pages record no evidence inputs.** `source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads` follows `list_sources`, `search_text` and `outline_source` through all their `next` pages. It asserts every delivery has empty `dependencies` and that the observation callback ran 0 times. `source_tools_forward_arguments_and_present_discovery_and_read_results` also asserts empty dependencies for discovery results, including a paged structural search.
- **Preparing an undelivered page records no read.** In `graph_tools_record_delivered_snapshots_and_prepared_pages_do_not_record_delivery`, an agent fails after a `read_node` was prepared. The test asserts `ctx.dependencies()` is empty. The final usage counts of prepared 6 and delivered 4 confirm the prepared page was never delivered. The `contents_of_current_node` case, where delivery does happen, records one dependency.

All of these tests carry `{test}` markers for the subject. I found no unmarked relevant test, no missing scenario, and no acknowledgments to consider.

text: :::{req} pages.inputs
A delivered read page records the dependencies retained by that page under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. Each continuation of a
node or mapped source read retains the original node identity and content
fingerprint; reading a later page does not observe a newer version. A change
to that node's fingerprint can invalidate the evidence even if it happens
between pages. Agent tools record on delivery. Discovery pages record no evidence
inputs, just like their initial result. Preparing an undelivered page records
no read.
:::{req} node_inputs
Finishing a verification includes every successful tracked node read in its
`Fingerprinted`, whether ordinary code or a model tool requested it. Each observation
contains the node identity and the fingerprint of the contents actually supplied.
A failed read returns an error without inventing a successful observation.
Repeating an identical observation adds no information. Reading the same
identity with two different fingerprints preserves both observations.
:::{req} pages.behavior
Each page has the same result fields as the originating tool. Text reads return
successive portions of text. Listings, outlines, and searches return successive
arrays of whole entries in their original order. Only a page with a successor
includes `next`.
Reusing a UUID returns the same page from the original snapshot, including the
same successor UUID if more remains. A malformed UUID, an unknown UUID, or a UUID
from another conversation returns a tool error under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.tool_agent.isolation`.
